children: Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRK.A) (NYSE:BRK.B), the insurance and investment conglomerate, disclosed that it bought about 2.74 million more Lennar shares. Berkshire stays flat at $507.01 at 11.27am ET time on Thursday

The filing records about 2.67 million Class A shares and 75,021 Class B shares bought across September 17, 18 and 21. At the disclosed weighted-average prices, the purchases cost an estimated $212.4 million, bringing Berkshire's holdings to 23.72 million Class A shares and 528,217 Class B shares. The chart shows Berkshire trading at $507.01, about 5.79% above its GuruFocus GF Value of $479.25.

That purchase is just 0.03% of Berkshire's market value, too small to move the needle for the conglomerate. The more telling detail is Berkshire crossing 10% ownership, which raises its reporting visibility and points to confidence in Lennar after weaker earnings. Whether this marks valuation-driven buying or the start of a larger stake will depend on Berkshire's next moves.

title: Berkshire Stays Flat as Lennar Stake Crosses 10%
